source.title: NPRA Guidelines for Control of Cosmetic Products in Malaysia (Second Edition) incl. Annex I Part 8 'Guideline for Cosmetic Claims' (Aug 2022); NPRA FAQ 'Control of Cosmetics Advertisement in Malaysia' (v1.0, Nov 2025)
source.citation: Guidelines §3.5 (Cosmetic Claims), §3.6 (Cosmetic Advertisement), §5.4 (Penalty, via s.30(1) CDCR 1984); Annex I Part 8 §3 (table of unacceptable / acceptable claims); NPRA FAQ Q2-Q10
source.last_reviewed_by: PENDING EXPERT REVIEW - transcribed from the primary NPRA documents by an AI assistant on 2026-09-20; not yet reviewed by a qualified Malaysian regulatory professional.

references.label: NPRA Guidelines for Control of Cosmetic Products in Malaysia (2nd ed.)
NPRA Annex I Part 8 - Guideline for Cosmetic Claims (Aug 2022)
NPRA FAQ - Control of Cosmetics Advertisement (Nov 2025)

permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable hair & scalp claim. NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8) §3, Hair & scalp.

permitted_claims.claim: Anti-hair loss / hair fall, or 'treatment / control of hair loss / hair fall'
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable only where hair fall is due to a physical factor such as hair breakage. Annex I Pt 8 §3, Hair & scalp.

permitted_claims.claim: Increase hair volume; promote healthy hair; helps strengthen / nourish hair root or hair follicle
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable. Volume claims must be due to the physical effect of the product (e.g. temporarily adding volume and body). Annex I Pt 8 §3.

permitted_claims.claim: Helps nourish / rejuvenate / regenerate cells; stimulate, increase or accelerate skin renewal; increase cell turnover; stimulates epidermal exfoliation; new fresh skin cells; younger looking skin
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable skin claims. Annex I Pt 8 §3, Skin products.

permitted_claims.claim: Slows down / delays signs of aging
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable. (Claiming to prevent, reduce, reverse or delay the aging PROCESS is not acceptable.) Annex I Pt 8 §3.

permitted_claims.claim: Prevent / control / reduce acne or breakouts
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable. (Claiming to heal, treat or stop acne is not acceptable.) Annex I Pt 8 §3.

permitted_claims.claim: Soften / treat hard skin, corns, callouses, cracked heels
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable. Annex I Pt 8 §3, Skin products.

permitted_claims.claim: Prevent / reduce dark spots, acne marks, wrinkles, pigmentation and stretch marks
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable wording. (Claiming to TREAT pigmentation, hyperpigmentation, freckles, melasma etc. is not.) Annex I Pt 8 §3.

permitted_claims.claim: Reduce / improve the appearance of cellulite; reduce / improve the appearance of scars
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable. (Preventing/treating cellulite or removing/eliminating scars is not.) Annex I Pt 8 §3.
Acceptable. (References to slimming, fat loss, fat burn, inch loss, draining/oedema are not.) Annex I Pt 8 §3.

permitted_claims.claim: Teeth whitening / bleaching; prevent gum problems; maintain healthy gums; relief of sensitive teeth; anti-cavity; anti-plaque; freshen breath
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable oral hygiene claims. Annex I Pt 8 §3, Oral hygiene products.

permitted_claims.claim: Prevent / eliminate body odour; reduce sweating
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable deodorant / anti-perspirant claims. Annex I Pt 8 §3.

permitted_claims.claim: Calming / relaxing / refreshing / uplifting; moisturizing / soothing (must be applied on skin)
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable for fragrance / essential-oil / aromatherapy products, provided claims stay within the cosmetic scope. Annex I Pt 8 §3.

permitted_claims.claim: Bust firming / lifting; prevent cracked nipple; moisturizing
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable bust product claims. Annex I Pt 8 §3.

permitted_claims.claim: Water / sweat resistant; prevent sunburn; UV filter; protect skin against harmful UVA & UVB rays; SPF 50+ (for SPF above 50)
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable sunscreen claims. Annex I Pt 8 §3.

permitted_claims.claim: Numerical performance claims such as '99.9%', 'in 3 days', '10x'
permitted_claims.notes: Acceptable ONLY if substantiated by relevant evidence. Annex I Pt 8, 'Other claims' (iv).

prohibited_claims.claim: Permanently eliminates / stops dandruff
prohibited_claims.reason: Cosmetics have temporary effects; permanent-cure wording is not an acceptable cosmetic claim.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Hair & scalp

prohibited_claims.claim: Hair loss can be arrested or reversed; restores hair cells; treats hereditary or hormonal hair loss, baldness or alopecia; prevent grey hair; treat cradle cap or seborrheic dermatitis
prohibited_claims.reason: Disease-treatment or physiological-function claims are not cosmetic claims.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Hair & scalp

prohibited_claims.claim: Stimulates / promotes hair growth (including 'grow hair in X days')
prohibited_claims.reason: Listed by NPRA as an unacceptable hair claim (acceptable alternatives: 'promote healthy hair', 'helps strengthen / nourish hair root or follicle').
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Hair & scalp

prohibited_claims.claim: References to collagen or elastin production, inhibition of melanin synthesis, DNA repair, skin metabolism, blood circulation or microcirculation
prohibited_claims.reason: Claims about internal biological/physiological mechanisms are unacceptable for cosmetics.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Skin products

prohibited_claims.claim: Prevent / reduce / reverse / delay the aging process (anti-aging as a process claim)
prohibited_claims.reason: Listed as unacceptable. Acceptable alternative: 'slows down / delays signs of aging'.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Skin products

prohibited_claims.claim: Heals, treats or stops acne
prohibited_claims.reason: Treatment claim. Acceptable alternative: 'prevent / control / reduce acne or breakouts'.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Skin products

prohibited_claims.claim: Treatment of warts
prohibited_claims.reason: Disease-treatment claim.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Skin products

prohibited_claims.claim: Treatment of skin conditions such as pigmentation, hyperpigmentation, freckles, melasma, acne, fragile capillaries, rosacea
prohibited_claims.reason: Treatment claim. Acceptable alternative: 'prevent / reduce dark spots, acne marks, wrinkles, pigmentation, stretch marks'.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Skin products

prohibited_claims.claim: Prevent / treat cellulite; remove / eliminate scars
prohibited_claims.reason: Listed as unacceptable. Acceptable alternatives: 'reduce / improve the appearance of cellulite / scars'.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Skin products

prohibited_claims.claim: Slimming, trimming, fat loss, fat burn, inch loss, body metabolism; removal of excess body fluid, draining, swelling or oedema
prohibited_claims.reason: Physiological / weight-management claims are not cosmetic claims. Acceptable alternative: 'body shaping, reshaping, contouring, firming'.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Skin products

prohibited_claims.claim: Treatment of compromised skin (bruises, wounds, burns); numbing effect on the skin
prohibited_claims.reason: Medicinal claims.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Skin products

prohibited_claims.claim: Reference to skin diseases (eczema, psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, vitiligo, varicose veins, rash, prickly heat, nappy rash) - e.g. 'cures eczema'
prohibited_claims.reason: Disease claims are explicitly unacceptable and NPRA lists them as a serious violation that can lead to cancellation of the product's notification.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Skin products; NPRA Cosmetics Advertisement FAQ (Nov 2025) Q7

prohibited_claims.claim: Treatment or prevention of oral diseases (dental abscess, gingivitis, mouth ulcers, periodontitis, stomatitis, thrush); gum bleeding; references to pain or nerves; increase saliva production; whitens tetracycline-induced stains
prohibited_claims.reason: Oral disease / medicinal claims are unacceptable for oral hygiene cosmetics.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Oral hygiene products

prohibited_claims.claim: Completely prevents or stops sweating / perspiration
prohibited_claims.reason: Listed as unacceptable. Acceptable alternative: 'reduce sweating'.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Deodorants & anti-perspirants

prohibited_claims.claim: Aphrodisiac / sexual attraction / hormonal attraction (fragrances, essential oils)
prohibited_claims.reason: Sexual-attraction and hormonal claims are unacceptable.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Perfumes / essential oil / aromatherapy

prohibited_claims.claim: Essential-oil or aromatherapy claims about illnesses or mental conditions: insomnia, anxiety, cold, flu, migraine, cough, respiratory problems, menopause, period pain, PMS, immune system, improved focus, memory enhancer, sleeping disorder, stress/tension relief; or 'to be taken / consumed'
prohibited_claims.reason: Reference to diseases, illness or mental wellbeing effects is outside the cosmetic scope; cosmetics must not be presented for ingestion.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Perfumes / essential oil / aromatherapy

prohibited_claims.claim: Relieves pain / ache of body, muscle or joint; stomach wind or bloating; improves blood circulation (massage products)
prohibited_claims.reason: Pain-relief and circulation claims are medicinal.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Products to assist body massage

prohibited_claims.claim: Feminine / male hygiene claims about sexual pleasure (e.g. tightening vaginal muscle), virility or sex drive, preserving normal flora, infection or inflammation, reducing vaginal discharge
prohibited_claims.reason: Sexual-function, infection and physiological claims are unacceptable.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Feminine / male hygiene products

prohibited_claims.claim: Bust enlargement / volumizing / size increase; reduce bust size
prohibited_claims.reason: Listed as unacceptable. Acceptable alternative: 'bust firming / lifting'.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Bust products

prohibited_claims.claim: Sunblock; sweat / water proof; UV block / cut; SPF above 50 (e.g. SPF 130); '100% protection'; references to skin cancer or reducing occurrence of cancer
prohibited_claims.reason: Absolute-protection and disease claims are unacceptable. Acceptable alternatives: 'water / sweat resistant', 'UV filter', 'SPF 50+'.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Sunscreen

prohibited_claims.claim: Stops / retards / prevents hair growth (depilatories)
prohibited_claims.reason: Listed as unacceptable. Acceptable: 'removes hair'.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Depilatories

prohibited_claims.claim: Antimicrobial, disinfectant, fungicidal / virucidal action; 'kills bacteria / germs' style claims outside approved antibacterial categories
prohibited_claims.reason: Listed as unacceptable general claims (see NPRA guidance for antibacterial hygiene wash and hand-sanitizer products separately).
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Others

prohibited_claims.claim: Reference to Hadith, Al-Quran, Bible or any religious statement; supernatural or superstitious elements (e.g. Saka, Sihir, Badi, Penawar)
prohibited_claims.reason: Religious and supernatural references are unacceptable on cosmetics.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Others and 'Other claims' (ii)

prohibited_claims.claim: Insect repellent (e.g. mozzie lotion, insect bite) claims
prohibited_claims.reason: Listed as unacceptable cosmetic claims.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Others

prohibited_claims.claim: Cosmeceutical; mesotherapy; injection; micro-needling; derma-roller; susuk
prohibited_claims.reason: Invasive / medicinal procedures and terms are unacceptable; NPRA lists ads for injection, mesotherapy, liposuction and micro-needling as serious violations.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Others; NPRA Cosmetics Advertisement FAQ (Nov 2025) Q7

prohibited_claims.claim: GMP logo / certification / ISO 22716 statements; 'Approved by Ministry of Health (MOH)'
prohibited_claims.reason: Unacceptable: manufacturer GMP marks and MOH-approval statements may not be used on cosmetic products.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Others and 'Other claims' (i)

prohibited_claims.claim: Medicated; used as gargle
prohibited_claims.reason: Medicinal descriptors are unacceptable for cosmetics.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Others

prohibited_claims.claim: Graphics, logos or symbols referring to internal organs, body parts or substances of human origin (Vagina, Growth Factor e.g. EGF & FGF, Capillary, Lymph, Spleen, Hormone, Nerve); indecent images
prohibited_claims.reason: Listed as unacceptable; ads that mention prohibited ingredients such as EGF/FGF, cannabis/hemp, oestrogens or progesterone are also treated as serious violations.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §3 - Others; NPRA Cosmetics Advertisement FAQ (Nov 2025) Q7

prohibited_claims.claim: 'No side effects', 'no harmful effects', 'no toxic or adverse effects'; implying a product is safe because it is natural
prohibited_claims.reason: Safety claims may not imply the product is free from side effects.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) - 'Other claims' (iii) Safety claims

prohibited_claims.claim: Doctors, pharmacists or dentists (or people/cartoons dressed as them: white coat, stethoscope, 'Dr.', clinic/hospital setting, 'Recommended by professionals') promoting or endorsing a cosmetic, including a medical professional's talk that ends with the product shown or mentioned
prohibited_claims.reason: NPRA states professional titles with clinical attire, or an impression of medical endorsement, are not allowed in cosmetic advertisements.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetics Advertisement FAQ (Nov 2025) Q2, Q4, Q6, Q10 (citing Guideline for Cosmetic Advertisement §4.1)

prohibited_claims.claim: A cosmetic name or claim that is medicinal in nature or beyond the cosmetic scope; presenting the product as treating or preventing disease
prohibited_claims.reason: General cosmetic-definition rule: presentation as treating or preventing disease makes the product a non-cosmetic.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Guidelines for Control of Cosmetic Products in Malaysia (2nd ed.) §3.5; Annex I Pt 8 §2(d)

restricted_or_conditional_claims.claim: Any benefit claim on a cosmetic (general rule)
restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: Claimed benefits must be justified by substantial evidence and/or by the formulation itself; the notification holder must be able to provide scientifically accepted study designs or data on request.
restricted_or_conditional_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Guidelines for Control of Cosmetic Products in Malaysia (2nd ed.) §3.5

restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: Acceptable only if substantiated by relevant evidence held by the notification holder.
restricted_or_conditional_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) - 'Other claims' (iv)

restricted_or_conditional_claims.claim: Secondary claims (dandruff, cellulite, bust contouring, hair loss, acne, caries, mouth wash, anti-bacterial)
restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: Acceptable as a secondary, minor function only, worded within the acceptable-claims list; the product's MAIN function must remain cleaning, perfuming, changing appearance, correcting odour, protecting or keeping in good condition.
restricted_or_conditional_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) §2(c)

restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: Non-GMP marks such as ECOCERT may be acceptable but must be substantiated; 'natural' must not suggest the product is safe because it is natural.
restricted_or_conditional_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline (Annex I Pt 8, Aug 2022) - 'Other claims' (i), (iii)

restricted_or_conditional_claims.claim: Sunscreen, hand sanitizer and antibacterial hygiene wash claims
restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: Governed by dedicated NPRA annexes (Annex I Part 9 (i)-(iii)); this tool only checks the general claims list above, so treat these as 'needs specialist review'.
restricted_or_conditional_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Guidelines for Control of Cosmetic Products in Malaysia (2nd ed.) §3.5

restricted_or_conditional_claims.claim: Advertisements published by distributors, agents, resellers or overseas headquarters
restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: No prior approval is required for cosmetic ads (self-regulation), but the notification holder is fully responsible for compliance, including ads by third parties and overseas HQ, and should get removal of non-compliant ads and keep records.
restricted_or_conditional_claims.regulation_reference: NPRA Cosmetics Advertisement FAQ (Nov 2025) - Introduction, Q8, Q9
